input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — walk-away territory under this rule, and well short of the fallback (single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty). It also conflicts with § 9.4 (our 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid Fees), § 7.1 (Fees per Order Form, no minimum-use charges) and § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment). Redline deletes the commitment and confirms Fees are due only for Services ordered or used, reaching the preferred position with a single-paragraph edit; a 12-month reducible commitment with a true-up is offered as fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year take-or-pay commitment; fees payable for Services ordered/used only.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced § 2.1 with fees for Services actually ordered or used, consistent with §§ 7.1, 9.4 and 12.3. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, and owes Fees only for Services ordered by Customer under an Order Form or actually used by Customer.
